title: Dedicated Serve Guarantee – Quantized Error Buckets, Preemptive Autoscale Clauses, and Contract Metrics
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Draft a contract-ready SLA model for dedicated GPU pools that combines (1) quantized error-buckets for measurable credits, (2) preemptive autoscale interlock language to reduce customer-visible degradations, and (3) clear measurement primitives that legal and finance can sign off on. Scope: this ticket covers definition of metrics, sample contract clauses, error-budget computation examples, ops runbook hooks (escalation + crediting), and a set of sample customer communications. Out of scope: final legal review, pricing negotiation templates (will be follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Concrete SLA metric(s) defined (e.g., committed_tokens_per_minute per tenant, p95 latency for small payloads, and availability window).
Error-budget computation algorithm specified with worked examples for 3 example customers (small, medium, enterprise).
Autoscale interlock behavior defined (trigger thresholds, cooldown, and preemptive burst credit consumption) and mapped to observable signals in Console.
Draft contract language (plain language + legal-friendly appendix) that legal and finance can review without significant rework.
Sample notification templates (notice windows, remediation timelines, customer crediting statement) included and linked to the recovery playbook.
decisions: Adopted 'quantized error-bucket' model: credits computed in discrete bands (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) rather than continuous percentages to simplify arbitration.

Primary throughput metric: committed_tokens_per_minute (CTPM) measured as 1-minute moving-window max, aggregated at tenant level per AZ. Secondary metric: p95 end-to-end generation latency for requests <= 512 tokens.
Autoscale interlock is preemptive: when forecasted burnrate approaches 85% of committed throughput for 3 consecutive minutes, we broaden autoscale policy (burst nodes) and flag for customer notice.

worked_examples: Example A (Small customer): committed 60k tokens/min. Observed 1-minute max of 45k -> no credit. Observed 1-minute max of 40k for 120 minutes in month -> credit band: 10% for 2 hours = prorated credit 0.28% of monthly commitment. Calculation in appendix.

Example B (Enterprise): committed 5M tokens/min. AZ outage reduces capacity to 3.8M for 30 minutes. Algorithm computes 25% band breach -> customer credited 25% of per-minute billing for the affected window with minimum 1-hour rounding.

Example C (Burst usage + Autoscale): customer committed 500k tokens/min but spikes to 800k for 7 minutes. Autoscale preemptive burst policy triggers at minute 3; customer consumes 3 minutes of 'burst credit' (customer-facing purchased burst units) then reverts to metrics-based credit computation for remaining 4 minutes.
example_clause_snippet:
Dedicated Serve Guarantee (excerpt):
We guarantee that the Dedicated Capacity will deliver at least the Committed Tokens Per Minute (CTPM) as stated in Section A. Credits are issued when measured CTPM falls into predefined bands against the commitment for the same AZ and billing account. Credit bands are: 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%. Credits are calculated per discrete minute and aggregated for the billing period.
Autoscale Interlock: Redwood will attempt preemptive autoscale actions when forecasted burnrate exceeds 85% of commitment for a sustained 3-minute window. Such actions are designed to reduce customer-visible errors and do not void credit eligibility unless the customer has elected and purchased an explicit 'best-effort burst' add-on.
risks: Measurement disagreement during multi-AZ failover may lead to disputed credits; need arbitration path + fallback to 5-minute windows.
Edge cases: very low-latency workloads with small payloads may inflate token measurement variance; requires a lower-bound smoothing filter.
Legal may require additional caps on total liability; potential negotiation impact on revenue.
